question: Where does the p95 tail live, and how big is it really?
headline: The tail was measured on a daemon carrying the idle-close defect, and it does
not reproduce on the build that fixes it. On the current build, 100 consecutive
gestures ran with zero failures at p50 544ms, p95 569ms, p99 590ms, max 709ms,
flat across the whole run.
So the honest number is p95 569ms, not the 3887ms recorded in
end-to-end-real-device.json. That file's tail figures describe the previous build.

whereTheTimeGoes.note: device legs measured spawned, at rest, immediately after the 100-gesture run
reading: A real tap costs the device ~427ms spawned and ~150ms more than a no-op, so
the same tap over the channel is roughly 350ms. Against a 544ms gesture that
leaves ~110ms for the identity check, the Runtime, XPC and the CLI together.
The injection itself is now the dominant term, and it is close to the whole
400ms budget on its own. Nothing above the device can bring the total under
the gate; only a cheaper injection can.

ruledOutByMeasurement: Capability store size: an engine run against an empty store and against the
maintainer's real 1.4 MB / 333-record document measured p50 87ms and 85ms.
Checkpointing: a whole-document write at 1.4 MB costs 17ms warm, 185ms cold.
Executable identity hashing: SHA-256 over the 6 MB hdc binary is 2.1ms.
F_FULLFSYNC: p50 3.0ms / p95 3.9ms at rest, and p50 3.0ms / p95 4.2ms sampled
throughout a gesture loop - no stall, 0 of 518 samples over 20ms.
Accumulated daemon state (1462 job directories, 1388 artifact directories) did
not prevent the 100-gesture run from being flat.
leadingHypothesisForTheOldTail: The only functional difference between the two builds is that a channel now gets
recycled instead of living forever. On the old build the channel that served
those batches had been open for tens of minutes across captures and idle spells.
A long-lived `hdc shell` degrading would produce what was seen: progressive
slowdown within a batch, recovery afterwards, and occasional target-list
dropouts. This is not proven - confirming it means holding one channel open for
twenty minutes and then bursting, which was not run.
methodNote: The first attribution experiment ran its three shapes sequentially rather than
interleaved, and concluded the tail was device-side. Interleaving reversed that
conclusion: the Runtime added p50 249ms and p95 1883ms over direct injection in
the one run where a tail appeared on the current build.
Sequential phases are not a controlled comparison when the device's own state
changes as the phases run - which it does, because every phase taps into a live
UI. Interleaving is what makes the two shapes comparable, and it is the practice
used everywhere else in this change.

gateStatus.verdict: not met, by ~145ms at p50 rather than by seconds
whatWouldClose it: The remaining gap is the injection itself. `uinput` costs ~279ms before it
injects anything and ~427ms for a real tap, spawned; the channel removes the
spawn but not the binary. A cheaper injection carrier is the only lever left
above 400ms, and finding one is not part of this change.
